title: Suryakumar Yadav Has Been Dropped From India's Asian Games Squad. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Is In.
excerpt: The BCCI's 30-member longlist for the Aichi-Nagoya Games excludes India's T20 captain. The decision was taken in January with the 2028 Olympics succession plan in mind.
body:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India has submitted a 30-member longlist of probable players to the Indian Olympic Association for the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The most significant name on the list is the one that is missing from it.

Suryakumar Yadav, India's reigning T20 World Cup-winning captain, has been excluded. According to a senior BCCI source quoted by the Times of India, the decision was taken all the way back in January. "It was decided in January that Suryakumar Yadav will not be part of the Asian Games," the source said. "The focus is on identifying his successor."

The omission is not a reaction to one bad IPL season. It is the beginning of a structured succession plan aimed at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the next T20 World Cup cycle.

## Why Suryakumar Was Left Out

Suryakumar's IPL 2026 form provides some context. Playing for Mumbai Indians, he scored 270 runs in 13 matches at an average of 20.77 — well below the standards that made him the ICC T20I Player of the Year in 2023 and 2024. His highest score was 60, and he managed only two half-centuries all season.

But the BCCI's decision goes beyond IPL form. With the 2028 Olympics including T20 cricket for the first time on the full programme, the selectors want to give potential successors as much competitive exposure as possible. The Asian Games, a multi-sport event played in a tournament T20 format, is the ideal proving ground.

"The government will prefer if the BCCI sends a full-strength team to the Asian Games," the source added. "A call on the Asian Games teams will be taken after consulting the government."

That last point is significant. The Indian government, which oversees Olympic sports through the Sports Ministry, has reportedly signalled its preference for a competitive squad — not a second-string developmental side.

## Shubman Gill's Absence Has a Different Explanation

India's Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill is also absent from the longlist, but for logistical reasons rather than selection ones. India's home series against the West Indies — three ODIs and five T20Is from September 27 to October 17 — overlaps with the Asian Games cricket tournament (September 24 to October 3). Gill is expected to lead the ODI squad against the West Indies, making it impossible for him to play in Aichi-Nagoya.

The BCCI is therefore preparing two separate T20 squads, one for each event, with some overlap in the player pool.

## Sooryavanshi Headlines the New Generation

The headline inclusion is fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. After guiding India's Under-19 team to a World Cup title with a 175 in the final, the left-handed opener produced one of the most extraordinary IPL debut seasons in history — 776 runs in 16 matches at a strike rate of 237.30 for Rajasthan Royals, including one century and three scores in the 90s.

His inclusion in the Asian Games longlist is the clearest signal yet that the BCCI views him not as a curiosity but as a central part of India's future.

## The Captaincy Race

With Suryakumar and Gill out of the picture, the Asian Games captaincy is an open contest. Three names have emerged as frontrunners:

**Shreyas Iyer** brings tactical maturity and leadership experience, having captained KKR to the IPL title in 2024. **Sanju Samson** offers senior T20 experience and has led Rajasthan Royals. **Tilak Varma**, the youngest of the three, has already captained India A and is seen as a long-term leadership prospect.

The final 15-member squad will be selected from the longlist in the second week of June.

## The Full Longlist

The 30 names submitted to the IOA: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson (wk), Shreyas Iyer, Rishabh Pant (wk), Hardik Pandya, Rinku Singh, Tilak Varma, Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Prasidh Krishna, Varun Chakravarthy, Anukul Roy, Ayush Badoni, Harsh Dubey, Dhruv Jurel, Khaleel Ahmed, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Ravi Bishnoi, Shahbaz Ahmed, Shivam Dube, Vipraj Nigam, Harshit Rana, Yash Thakur, Washington Sundar.

## What It Means for the Diaspora Fan

For NRI cricket fans who have followed Suryakumar Yadav's rise from Mumbai's domestic circuit to become one of the world's most thrilling T20 batters, his omission is jarring even if the reasoning is sound. The BCCI is making a calculated bet that the short-term cost of dropping a proven match-winner is worth the long-term gain of building a team for 2028.

Whether that bet pays off will depend on who emerges from the Asian Games as India's next T20 leader. The selectors have given themselves a list of thirty to choose from. By June, they will need to narrow it to fifteen — and in doing so, they will be choosing not just a squad, but a direction.
nri_angle: The BCCI dropping T20 captain Suryakumar Yadav from the Asian Games longlist signals a generational shift in Indian cricket. For NRI fans who watched SKY become a global T20 icon, this is the beginning of the post-Suryakumar era — with fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi leading the charge.
